name: P2 · Unit 2 — Discrete Structures & Optimization (complete)
description: All 9 topics of Unit 2 split into 30 syllabus sub-topics, 30 questions each: propositional and predicate logic, inference, sets, relations, counting, induction, probability, Bayes, graph theory, planarity, colouring, trees, prefix codes, traversals, spanning trees, Boolean algebra. Many worked numericals.

questions.question: Which of the following is a proposition?
questions.subject: Propositional Logic
questions.explanation: A proposition is a declarative sentence that is either true or false. '2 + 3 = 7' is false but is still a proposition; 'x + 1 = 5' depends on x.

questions.question: The conditional p → q is false only when:

options.C: p is true and q is false

questions.subject: Propositional Logic
questions.explanation: An implication fails only when a true hypothesis leads to a false conclusion.

questions.question: The contrapositive of p → q is:
questions.subject: Propositional Logic
questions.explanation: q → p is the converse and ¬p → ¬q is the inverse.

questions.question: Which of the following is logically equivalent to p → q?
questions.subject: Propositional Logic
questions.explanation: An implication and its contrapositive always have the same truth value.

questions.question: The contrapositive of 'If it rains, then the ground is wet' is:

options.A: If it does not rain, then the ground is not wet
options.B: If the ground is wet, then it rains

questions.explanation: p ∨ ¬p is always true (law of excluded middle).

questions.question: Which of the following is a contradiction?
questions.subject: Propositional Logic
questions.explanation: p ∧ ¬p is always false.

questions.subject: Propositional Logic
questions.explanation: Its truth value depends on the values of its variables, e.g. p → q.

options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Propositional Equivalences
questions.explanation: Since {¬, ∧} is functionally complete and both can be built from NAND, NAND alone is complete.

questions.question: The Principal Disjunctive Normal Form (PDNF) of a formula is a:

questions.explanation: Each maxterm corresponds to a row where the formula is false.

questions.question: How many minterms are possible in n propositional variables?

questions.question: The minterm corresponding to p = T, q = F, r = T is:
questions.subject: Normal Forms
questions.explanation: A minterm is true for exactly that one assignment.

questions.question: The complement of F = xy + z is:

questions.question: The 3-variable majority function Σm(3, 5, 6, 7) can be written as:
questions.subject: Boolean Functions and their Representation
questions.explanation: It is 1 when at least two inputs are 1.

questions.question: By the consensus theorem, xy + x'z + yz equals:
questions.subject: Boolean Functions and their Representation
questions.explanation: The consensus term yz is redundant.

questions.question: The number of elements of any finite Boolean algebra is always:

options.B: Even but not necessarily a power of 2

questions.subject: Boolean Functions and their Representation
questions.explanation: It is isomorphic to the power set of some finite set.

questions.question: Which single gate type is functionally complete?
questions.subject: Boolean Functions and their Representation
questions.explanation: NOR is also functionally complete.

questions.question: A two-level AND–OR circuit directly implements an expression in:
questions.subject: Boolean Functions and their Representation
questions.explanation: AND gates form the products and an OR gate sums them.

questions.question: How many minterms does F(x, y) = x + y have?
questions.subject: Boolean Functions and their Representation
questions.explanation: It is 1 for the rows 01, 10 and 11.

questions.question: The canonical SOP (sum of minterms) form of a Boolean function is:
questions.subject: Boolean Functions and their Representation
questions.explanation: Each function has exactly one set of minterms.

questions.question: XNOR of x and y equals 1 when:
questions.subject: Boolean Functions and their Representation
questions.explanation: It is the complement of XOR.

questions.question: In Boolean algebra, x · (x + y) equals:
questions.subject: Boolean Functions and their Representation
questions.explanation: This is the dual absorption law.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. In Boolean algebra, x + yz = (x + y)(x + z).
II. In Boolean algebra, x(y + z) = xy + xz.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Boolean Functions and their Representation
questions.explanation: Both distributive laws hold in Boolean algebra (unlike ordinary arithmetic, where only II holds).

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The dual of x + 0 = x is x · 1 = x.
Reason (R): Duality interchanges + with · and 0 with 1.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Boolean Functions and their Representation
questions.explanation: Applying R to the identity gives A.

questions.question: xy + xy' simplifies to:
questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: x(y + y') = x.

questions.question: (x + y)(x + y') simplifies to:
questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: x + yy' = x.

questions.question: xyz + xyz' + xy'z simplifies to:
questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: xy(z + z') + xy'z = xy + xy'z = x(y + y'z) = x(y + z).

questions.question: In a Karnaugh map, the columns for two variables are labelled in the order 00, 01, 11, 10 because:

options.B: Adjacent cells must differ in exactly one variable (Gray code)

questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: This makes adjacency visible.

questions.question: Groups of 1s in a K-map must contain how many cells?
questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: Each doubling eliminates one variable.

questions.question: Simplify F(x, y, z) = Σm(0, 2, 4, 6).
questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: These are exactly the rows where z = 0.

questions.question: Simplify F(x, y, z) = Σm(0, 1, 2, 3).
questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: These are the rows where x = 0.

questions.question: Simplify F(x, y, z) = Σm(3, 5, 6, 7).
questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: The majority function needs three groups of two.

questions.question: Simplify F(w, x, y, z) = Σm(0, 2, 8, 10).
questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: The four corner cells of a 4-variable K-map group together: x = 0 and z = 0.

questions.question: Simplify F(w, x, y, z) = Σm(0, 1, …, 15).
questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: All cells are 1.

questions.question: Simplify F(w, x, y, z) = Σm(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7).
questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: These are all the rows with w = 0.

questions.question: Simplify F(x, y, z) = Σm(1, 2, 3, 5, 7).
questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: z covers 1, 3, 5, 7 and x'y covers 2 and 3.

questions.question: Simplify x'y'z' + x'y'z + x'yz.
questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: Minterms 0, 1, 3: x'y' covers 0 and 1; x'z covers 1 and 3.

questions.question: 'Don't care' conditions in a K-map:

options.A: May be treated as 0 or 1, whichever gives a simpler expression

questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: E.g. the unused BCD codes 1010–1111.

questions.question: A prime implicant is:

options.C: A product term (group) that cannot be combined into a larger group

questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: Essential prime implicants cover some minterm that no other prime implicant covers.

questions.question: An essential prime implicant is one that:

options.A: Covers at least one minterm not covered by any other prime implicant

questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: It must appear in every minimal SOP.

questions.question: Which method is systematic and suitable for simplifying functions with many variables by computer?
questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: K-maps become impractical beyond 5–6 variables.

questions.question: A 4-variable K-map has how many cells?
questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions

questions.question: In a 4-variable K-map, a group of 8 adjacent 1s produces a term with how many literals?
questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: 8 = 2³ eliminates 3 of the 4 variables.

questions.question: In a 4-variable K-map, a group of 4 adjacent 1s produces a term with how many literals?
questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: 4 = 2² eliminates 2 variables.

questions.question: For POS simplification using a K-map, you group:
questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: Grouping the 0s gives F', which is complemented into POS form.

questions.question: For variables (x, y), F = ΠM(0, 1) simplifies to:
questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: F is 0 exactly when x = 0, so F = x.

questions.question: A two-level SOP circuit can be implemented using only:
questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: AND–OR is equivalent to NAND–NAND.

questions.question: A two-level POS circuit can be implemented using only:
questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: OR–AND is equivalent to NOR–NOR.

questions.question: (x + y)(x' + z)(y + z) simplifies to:
questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: This is the dual of the consensus theorem.

questions.question: Why can x ⊕ y = x'y + xy' not be simplified further on a K-map?

options.B: Its 1s are diagonal (checkerboard) and no two are adjacent

questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: Parity functions are the worst case for K-map simplification.

questions.question: In a 3-variable K-map, which pair of cells is adjacent?
questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: 001 and 011 differ in one variable only.

questions.question: In a 4-variable K-map, the cells in the leftmost and rightmost columns of a row are:

options.A: Adjacent only in the first row

questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: The map is effectively a torus.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Every essential prime implicant must appear in the minimal SOP expression.
II. Every prime implicant must appear in the minimal SOP expression.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: Some prime implicants are redundant, e.g. consensus terms.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A group of 6 adjacent 1s can be used as one term in a K-map.
Reason (R): Every group in a K-map must contain 2^k cells.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Simplification of Boolean Functions
questions.explanation: A is false because 6 is not a power of 2; R is true.
